分散-收集模式

Scatter/Gather with Root Distribution Hands On: Distributed Document Search Scatter/Gather with Leaf Sharding Hands On: Sharded Document Search Choosing the Right Number of Leaves Scaling Scatter/Gather for Reliability and Scale Summary

Scatter/Gather分散-收集模式

— PDF 第 101 页 —

So far we’ve examined systems that replicate for scalability in terms of the number of requests processed per second (the stateless replicated pattern), as well as scalability for the size of the data (the sharded data pattern). In this chapter we introduce the scatter/gather pattern, which uses replication for scalability in terms of time. Specifically, the scatter/gather pattern allows you to achieve parallelism in servicing requests, enabling you to service them significantly faster than you could if you had to service them sequentially.

到目前为止，我们已经考察了两类系统：一类为每秒处理请求数的可扩展性而复制（无状态复制模式），另一类为数据规模的可扩展性而分片（分片数据模式）。本章介绍分散-收集模式，它利用复制来获得时间维度上的可扩展性。具体而言，分散-收集模式让你在服务请求时实现并行，从而比顺序服务请求快得多。

Like replicated and sharded systems, the scatter/gather pattern is a tree pattern with a root that distributes requests and leaves that process those requests. However, in contrast to replicated and sharded systems, scatter/gather requests are simultaneously farmed out to all of the replicas in the system. Each replica does a small amount of processing and then returns a fraction of the result to the root. The root server then combines the various partial results together to form a single complete response to the request and then sends this request back out to the client. The scatter/gather pattern is illustrated in Figure 8-1.

与复制系统和分片系统一样，分散-收集模式也是一种树形模式：有一个分发请求的根节点，以及处理请求的叶子节点。然而，与复制系统和分片系统不同，分散-收集请求会被同时分发到系统中的所有副本。每个副本做一小部分处理，然后把结果的一小部分返回给根节点。根服务器随后把各个部分结果合并起来，形成对该请求的一个完整响应，再把这个响应发回给客户端。分散-收集模式如图 8-1 所示。

— PDF 第 102 页 —

Scatter/gather is quite useful when you have a large amount of mostly independent processing that is needed to handle a particular request. With such problems, it is relatively easy to spread the computation required across multiple different independent processors.

当处理某个特定请求需要大量、彼此基本独立的处理时，分散-收集非常有用。对于这类问题，把所需计算分摊到多个相互独立的处理器上相对容易。

Whereas the previous examples of caching sharded the data to maximize the efficiency of memory usage, the scatter/gather algorithm shards the computation necessary to service the request, reducing the latency via parallel processing. Though sometimes, as we will see, the data is sharded as well.

前面的缓存示例通过对数据分片来最大化内存使用效率，而分散-收集算法则对服务请求所需的计算进行分片，通过并行处理来降低延迟。不过正如我们将看到的，有时数据也会被分片。

Scatter/Gather with Root Distribution根节点分发的分散-收集

The simplest form of scatter/gather is one in which each leaf is entirely homogenous but the work is distributed to a number of different leaves in order to improve the performance of the request. This pattern is equivalent to solving an “embarrassingly parallel” problem. The problem can be broken up into many different pieces, and each piece can be put back together with all of the other pieces to form a complete answer.

最简单的分散-收集形式，是每个叶子节点完全同质，但为了提升请求性能，工作被分发到多个不同的叶子节点上。这种模式等价于求解一个“极易并行化”的问题。该问题可以被拆成许多不同的片段，每个片段都能与其他片段重新拼合，形成一个完整答案。

To understand this in more concrete terms, imagine that you need to service a user request R, and it takes one minute for a single core to produce the answer A to this request. If we program a multithreaded application, we can parallelize this request on a single machine by using multiple cores. Given this approach and a 30-core processor (yes, typically it would be a 32-core processor, but 30 makes the math cleaner), we can reduce the time that it takes to process a single request down to 2 seconds (60 seconds of computation split across 30 threads for computation is equal to 2 seconds). But even 2 seconds is pretty slow to service a user’s web request.

为了更具体地理解，请设想：你需要服务一个用户请求 R，单核需要一分钟才能得出该请求的答案 A。如果我们编写一个多线程应用，就可以在单机上用多核把这个请求并行化。采用这种方法，配上一颗 30 核处理器（是的，通常会是 32 核，但 30 让数字算起来更干净），我们就能把处理单个请求的时间降到 2 秒（60 秒计算量分摊到 30 个计算线程上，等于 2 秒）。但即便 2 秒，对服务一个用户的 Web 请求来说也相当慢了。

— PDF 第 103 页 —

Additionally, truly achieving a completely parallel speed-up on a single process is going to be tricky, as things like memory, network, or disk bandwidth start to become the bottleneck. Instead of (or in addition to) parallelizing an application across cores on a single machine, we can use the scatter/gather pattern to parallelize requests across multiple processes on many different machines. In this way, we can improve our overall latency requests, since we are no longer bound by the number of cores we can get on a single machine, as well as ensure that the bottleneck in our process continues to be CPU, since the memory, network, and disk bandwidth are all spread across a number of different machines. Additionally, because every machine in the scatter/gather tree is capable of handling every request, the root of the tree can dynamically dispatch load to different nodes at different times depending on their responsiveness. If, for some reason, a particular leaf node is responding more slowly than other machines (e.g., it has a noisy neighbor process that is interfering with resources), then the root can dynamically redistribute load to assure a fast response.

此外，要在单进程上真正实现完全的并行加速并不容易，因为内存、网络或磁盘带宽等会开始成为瓶颈。我们可以（代替或补充单机多核并行）用分散-收集模式，把请求并行化到许多不同机器上的多个进程中。这样一来，我们既能改善整体请求延迟——因为不再受单机可获得的核数限制——又能保证进程的瓶颈继续是 CPU，因为内存、网络和磁盘带宽都分散到了多台不同机器上。此外，由于分散-收集树中的每台机器都能处理每一个请求，树根可以根据各节点的响应能力，在不同时间动态地把负载派发到不同节点。如果某个叶子节点由于某种原因比其他机器响应更慢（例如它有一个“吵闹邻居”进程在争抢资源），根节点就可以动态地重新分配负载，以保证快速响应。

Hands On: Distributed Document Search实战：分布式文档搜索

To see an example of scatter/gather in action, consider the task of searching across a large database of documents for all documents that contain the words “cat” and “dog.” One way to perform this search would be to open up all of the documents, read through the entire set, searching for the words in each document, and then return to the user the set of documents that contain both words.

为了看一个分散-收集实际运作的例子，请设想这样一个任务：在一个大型文档库中搜索所有同时包含单词“cat”和“dog”的文档。执行这种搜索的一种方式是：打开所有文档，通读整个集合，在每个文档中搜索这两个词，然后把同时包含这两个词的文档集合返回给用户。

As you might imagine, this is quite a slow process because it requires opening and reading through a large number of files for each request. To make request processing faster, you can build an index. Just like in the back of a reference book, the index is effectively a hashtable, where the keys are individual words (e.g., “cat”) and the values are a list of documents (or pages) containing that word.

你可以想象，这是一个相当慢的过程，因为每个请求都要打开并通读大量文件。为了加快请求处理，你可以建一个索引。就像参考书末尾的索引一样，这个索引实际上是一个哈希表：键是单个单词（例如“cat”），值是包含该词的文档（或页面）列表。

Now, instead of searching through every document, finding the documents that match any one word is as easy as doing a lookup in this hashtable. However, we have lost one important ability. Remember that we were looking for all documents that contained “cat” and “dog.” Since the index only has single words, not conjunctions of words, we still need to find the documents that contain both words. Luckily, this is just an intersection of the sets of documents returned for each word.

现在，不必通读每个文档，找到匹配任意一个词的文档就像在这个哈希表里查一下一样简单。然而，我们失去了一项重要能力。别忘了，我们要找的是同时包含“cat”和“dog”的所有文档。由于索引里只有单个词、没有词的组合，我们仍需找出同时包含这两个词的文档。幸运的是，这只是对每个词所返回文档集合求交集。

We could implement this algorithm on a single machine. Step one would be to use the index to look up the list of documents containing cat. Step two would be to use the index to look up the list of documents containing dog. And the final step would be to find the intersection, the documents which are present in both lists. Looking at these steps, it’s clear that the lookup for cat and the lookup for dog are independent; they can easily be performed in parallel and can even be performed on different machines. Calculating the intersection, however, requires both lists of documents, and thus is dependent on the data from the first two steps.

我们可以在单机上实现这个算法。第一步，用索引查出包含 cat 的文档列表。第二步，用索引查出包含 dog 的文档列表。最后一步，求交集——即同时出现在两个列表中的文档。看这几步就会发现，查 cat 和查 dog 显然是相互独立的；它们可以很容易地并行执行，甚至可以在不同机器上执行。然而，计算交集需要两个文档列表，因此依赖于前两步的数据。

— PDF 第 104 页 —

Given this understanding, we can implement this document search as an example of the scatter/gather pattern. When a request comes in to the document search root, it parses the request and farms out to two leaf machines (one for the word “cat” and one for the word “dog”). Each of these machines returns a list of documents that match one of the words, and the root node returns the list of documents containing both “cat” and “dog.”

理解了这一点，我们就可以把这个文档搜索实现为分散-收集模式的一个例子。当请求到达文档搜索根节点时，它解析请求，并把任务分发到两台叶子机器（一台查“cat”，一台查“dog”）。每台机器返回匹配其中一个词的文档列表，根节点则返回同时包含“cat”和“dog”的文档列表。

A diagram of this process is shown in Figure 8-2: the leaf returns {doc1, doc2, doc4} for “cat” and {doc1, doc3, doc4} for “dog,” so the root finds the intersection and returns {doc1, doc4}.

这个过程如图 8-2 所示：叶子节点对“cat”返回 {doc1, doc2, doc4}，对“dog”返回 {doc1, doc3, doc4}，于是根节点求交集并返回 {doc1, doc4}。

Scatter/Gather with Leaf Sharding叶子分片的分散-收集

While applying the replicated data scatter/gather pattern allows you to reduce the processing time required for handling user requests, it doesn’t allow you to scale beyond an amount of data that can be held in the memory or disk of a single machine. Much like the replicated serving pattern that was previously described, it is simple to build a replicated scatter/gather system. But at a certain data size, it is necessary to introduce sharding in order to build a system that can hold more data than can be stored on a single machine.

应用复制数据的分散-收集模式虽然能减少处理用户请求所需的时间，但它无法让你扩展到超出单机内存或磁盘所能容纳的数据量。与前面描述的复制服务模式很像，构建一个复制的分散-收集系统很简单。但当数据量达到一定规模时，就必须引入分片，才能构建一个容纳数据量超过单机存储能力的系统。

Previously, when sharding was introduced to scale replicated systems, the sharding was done at a per-request level. Some part of the request was used to determine where the request was sent. That replica then handled all of the processing for the request, and the response was handed back to the user. Instead, with scatter/gather sharding, the request is sent to all of the leaf nodes (or shards) in the system. Each leaf node processes the request using the data that it has loaded in its shard. This partial response is then returned to the root node that requested data, and that root node merges all of the responses together to form a comprehensive response for the user.

前面，当我们为扩展复制系统而引入分片时，分片是按请求维度做的：用请求的某一部分来决定把请求发到哪里，然后那个副本处理该请求的全部工作，再把响应交还给用户。而在分散-收集分片中，请求会被发送到系统中的所有叶子节点（即分片）。每个叶子节点用自己分片里加载的数据来处理该请求。这个部分响应随后被返回给发起请求的根节点，根节点再把所有响应合并起来，形成一个面向用户的完整响应。

— PDF 第 105 页 —

As a concrete example of this sort of architecture, consider implementing search across a very large document set (all patents in the world, for example); in such a case, the data is too large to fit in the memory of a single machine, so instead the data is sharded across multiple replicas. For example, patents 0–100,000 might be on the first machine, 100,001–200,000 on the next machine, and so forth. (Note that this is not actually a good sharding scheme since it will continually force us to add new shards as new patents are registered. In practice, we’d likely use the patent number modulo the total number of shards.)

作为这种架构的一个具体例子，请设想在一个非常大的文档集合上实现搜索（例如全世界的所有专利）；在这种情况下，数据太大，装不进单机内存，于是数据被分片到多个副本上。例如，专利 0–100,000 可能在第一台机器上，100,001–200,000 在下一台机器上，依此类推。（注意，这其实并不是一个好的分片方案，因为随着新专利注册，它会不断迫使我们添加新分片。实践中，我们很可能用专利号对总分片数取模。）

When a user submits a request to find a particular word (e.g., “rockets”) in all of the patents in the index, that request is sent to each shard, which searches through its patent shard for patents that match the word in the query. Any matches that are found are returned to the root node in response to the shard request. The root node then collates all of these responses together into a single response that contains all the patents that match the particular word. The operation of this search index is illustrated in Figure 8-3.

当用户提交请求，要在索引中的所有专利里查找某个特定词（例如“rockets”）时，该请求会被发送到每个分片，每个分片在自己的专利分片中搜索匹配查询词的专利。任何匹配项都会作为对分片请求的响应返回给根节点。根节点随后把所有这些响应整理合并成一个响应，其中包含所有匹配该特定词的专利。这个搜索索引的运作如图 8-3 所示。

Hands On: Sharded Document Search实战：分片文档搜索

The previous example scattered the different term requests across the cluster, but this only works if all of the documents are present on all of the machines in the scatter/gather tree. If there is not enough room for all of the documents in all of the leaves in the tree, then sharding must be used to put different sets of documents onto different leaves.

前面那个例子把不同的词项请求分散到整个集群，但这只有在分散-收集树中所有机器上都存有全部文档时才行得通。如果树中所有叶子节点的空间不足以容纳全部文档，就必须用分片把不同的文档集放到不同的叶子上。

This means that when a user makes a request for all documents that match the words “cat” and “dog,” the request is actually sent out to every leaf in the scatter/gather system. Each leaf node returns the set of documents that it knows about that matches “cat” and “dog.” Previously, the root node was responsible for performing the intersection of the two sets of documents returned for two different words. In the sharded case, the root node is responsible for generating the union of all of the documents returned by all of the different shards and returning this complete set of documents back up to the user.

这意味着，当用户请求所有匹配“cat”和“dog”的文档时，该请求实际上被发送到分散-收集系统中的每一个叶子。每个叶子节点返回它所知道的、匹配“cat”和“dog”的文档集合。前面，根节点负责对两个不同词所返回的两个文档集合求交集。而在分片情况下，根节点负责把所有不同分片返回的所有文档取并集，并把这个完整的文档集合返回给用户。

In Figure 8-3, the first leaf serves documents 1 through 10 and returns {doc1, doc5}. The second leaf serves documents 11 through 20 and returns {doc15}. The third leaf serves documents 21 through 30 and returns {doc22, doc28}. The root combines all of these responses together into a single response and returns {doc1, doc5, doc15, doc22, doc28}.

在图 8-3 中，第一个叶子服务文档 1 到 10，返回 {doc1, doc5}；第二个叶子服务文档 11 到 20，返回 {doc15}；第三个叶子服务文档 21 到 30，返回 {doc22, doc28}。根节点把所有这些响应合并成一个响应，返回 {doc1, doc5, doc15, doc22, doc28}。

— PDF 第 106 页 —

Choosing the Right Number of Leaves选择合适的叶子节点数量

It might seem that in the scatter/gather pattern, replicating out to a very large number of leaves would always be a good idea. You parallelize your computation and consequently reduce the clock time required to process any particular request. However, increased parallelization comes at a cost, and thus choosing the right number of leaf nodes in the scatter/gather pattern is critical to designing a performant distributed system.

在分散-收集模式中，把副本扩展到非常多的叶子节点似乎总是个好主意。你把计算并行化，从而减少处理任一特定请求所需的时钟时间。然而，提高并行度是有代价的，因此在分散-收集模式中选择合适的叶子节点数量，对设计高性能分布式系统至关重要。

To understand how this can happen, it’s worth considering two things. The first is that processing any particular request has a certain amount of overhead. This includes the time spent parsing a request, sending requests across the network, and performing encryption. In general, the overhead due to system request handling is constant and significantly less than the time spent in user code processing the request. Consequently, this overhead can generally be ignored when assessing the performance of the scatter/gather pattern. However, it is important to understand that you pay the cost of this overhead on every leaf node in the scatter/gather system. Each leaf node you add to increase parallelism increases the total overhead cost.

要理解为什么会这样，有两点值得考虑。第一，处理任何特定请求都有一定的开销，包括解析请求、跨网络发送请求以及加解密所花的时间。一般来说，系统请求处理带来的开销是恒定的，且远小于用户代码处理请求所花的时间。因此，在评估分散-收集模式的性能时，这种开销通常可以忽略。但重要的是要明白：你在分散-收集系统的每个叶子节点上都要付出这份开销。你每增加一个叶子节点来提高并行度，总开销成本就随之增加。

Additionally, increasing the parallelism reduces the time spent performing “useful” computation on each leaf node, until eventually the time spent on the computational overhead is significantly greater than the time spent performing “useful” computation. When this happens, you can no longer improve performance by adding additional leaf nodes. This means that the gains of parallelization are asymptotic. You cannot continually add nodes and expect to improve performance.

此外，提高并行度会减少每个叶子节点上花在“有用”计算上的时间，直到最终花在计算开销上的时间明显超过花在“有用”计算上的时间。当这种情况发生时，你再增加叶子节点也无法提升性能。这意味着并行化的收益是渐近的：你不能不断加节点就指望性能持续提升。

In addition to the fact that adding more leaf nodes may not actually speed up processing, scatter/gather systems also suffer from the “straggler” problem, which you may have encountered in MapReduce big-data systems like Hadoop. To understand how this works, it is important to remember that in a scatter/gather system, the root node waits for requests from all of the leaf nodes to return before sending a response back to the end user.

除了增加叶子节点未必真能加快处理之外，分散-收集系统还受“拖后腿者”（straggler）问题的困扰——你可能在 Hadoop 这类 MapReduce 大数据系统中遇到过。要理解这是怎么回事，重要的是记住：在分散-收集系统中，根节点要等所有叶子节点的请求都返回后，才会向终端用户发回响应。

— PDF 第 107 页 —

Since data from every leaf node is required, the overall time it takes to process a user request is defined by the slowest leaf node that sends a response. To understand the impact of this, imagine that we have a service that has a 99th percentile latency of 2 seconds. This means that on average one request out of every 100 has a latency of 2 seconds, or put another way, there is a 1% chance that a request will take 2 seconds. This may be totally acceptable at first glance: a single user out of 100 has a slow request. However, consider how this actually works in a scatter/gather system. Since the time of the user request is defined by the slowest response, we need to consider not a single request but all requests scattered out to the various leaf nodes.

由于需要每个叶子节点的数据，处理一个用户请求的总时间由最慢的那个返回响应的叶子节点决定。要理解其影响，请设想我们有一个服务，其第 99 百分位延迟为 2 秒。这意味着平均每 100 个请求中就有 1 个延迟为 2 秒；换句话说，一个请求耗时 2 秒的概率是 1%。乍看之下这完全可以接受：每 100 个用户中只有 1 个遇到慢请求。然而，请考虑这在分散-收集系统中实际是怎么回事。由于用户请求的时间由最慢的响应决定，我们需要考虑的不是单个请求，而是分散到各个叶子节点上的所有请求。

Let’s see what happens when we scatter out to five leaf nodes. In this situation, there is a 5% chance that one of these five scatter requests has a latency of 2 seconds (0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 = 0.95). This means that our 99th percentile latency for individual requests becomes a 95th percentile latency for our complete scatter/gather system. And it only gets worse from there: if we scatter out to 100 leaves, then we are more or less guaranteeing that our overall latency for all requests will be 2 seconds.

我们来看看分散到 5 个叶子节点时会发生什么。在这种情况下，这 5 个分散请求中有一个延迟为 2 秒的概率是 5%（0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 × 0.99 = 0.95）。这意味着单个请求原本的第 99 百分位延迟，在整个分散-收集系统中变成了第 95 百分位延迟。而且情况只会更糟：如果我们分散到 100 个叶子节点，那几乎就是在保证所有请求的整体延迟都是 2 秒。

Together, these complications of scatter/gather systems lead us to some conclusions:

综合来看，分散-收集系统的这些复杂问题把我们引向如下结论：

  • Increased parallelism doesn’t always speed things up because of overhead on each node.由于每个节点上的开销，提高并行度并不总能加快速度。
  • Increased parallelism doesn’t always speed things up because of the straggler problem.由于拖后腿者问题，提高并行度并不总能加快速度。
  • The performance of the 99th percentile is more important than in other systems because each user request actually becomes numerous requests to the service.第 99 百分位性能比在其他系统中更重要，因为每个用户请求实际上变成了对服务的众多请求。

The same straggler problem applies to availability. If you issue a request to 100 leaf nodes, and the probability that any leaf node failing is 1 in 100, you are again practically guaranteed to fail every single user request.

同样的拖后腿者问题也适用于可用性。如果你向 100 个叶子节点发出请求，而任意一个叶子节点故障的概率是百分之一，那么你几乎可以说必然会让每一个用户请求都失败。

Scaling Scatter/Gather for Reliability and Scale为可靠性与规模扩展分散-收集

Of course, just as with a sharded system, having a single replica of a sharded scatter/gather system is likely not the desirable design choice. A single replica means that if it fails, all scatter/gather requests will fail for the duration that the shard is unavailable because all requests are required to be processed by all leaf nodes in the scatter/gather pattern. Likewise, upgrades will take out a percentage of your shards, so an upgrade while under user-facing load is no longer possible. Finally, the computational scale of your system will be limited by the load that any single node is capable of achieving. Ultimately, this limits your scale, and as we have seen in previous sections, you cannot simply increase the number of shards in order to improve the computational power of a scatter/gather pattern.

当然，与分片系统一样，让分片的分散-收集系统只有单个副本，很可能不是理想的设计选择。单副本意味着：一旦它故障，在该分片不可用期间，所有分散-收集请求都会失败，因为在分散-收集模式中，所有请求都必须由所有叶子节点处理。同样，升级会让一部分分片下线，因此在面向用户的负载下进行升级就不再可能。最后，系统的计算规模会受限于单个节点所能达到的负载。归根结底，这会限制你的规模；而正如我们在前几节看到的，你不能简单地增加分片数量来提升分散-收集模式的计算能力。

— PDF 第 108 页 —

Given these challenges of reliability and scale, the correct approach is to replicate each of the individual shards so that instead of a single instance at each leaf node, there is a replicated service that implements each leaf shard. This replicated sharded scatter/gather pattern is shown in Figure 8-4.

面对这些可靠性与规模上的挑战，正确的做法是对每个分片分别进行复制，使得每个叶子节点处不再是单实例，而是由一个复制服务来实现每个叶子分片。这种复制的分片分散-收集模式如图 8-4 所示。

Built this way, each leaf request from the root is actually load balanced across all healthy replicas of the shard. This means that if there are any failures, they won’t result in a user-visible outage for your system. Likewise, you can safely perform an upgrade under load, since each replicated shard can be upgraded one replica at a time. Indeed, you can perform the upgrade across multiple shards simultaneously, depending on how quickly you want to perform the upgrade.

这样构建后，根节点发来的每个叶子请求，实际上会被负载均衡到该分片的所有健康副本上。这意味着即便发生故障，也不会造成用户可见的系统中断。同样，你可以在负载下安全地进行升级，因为每个复制分片可以一次升级一个副本。事实上，你还可以跨多个分片同时升级，这取决于你希望升级得多快。

Summary小结

This chapter describes the scatter/gather pattern, a distributed system for improving computation speed and reducing the latency of handling any particular request. Whereas previous serving patterns focused on scaling for additional load or scaling for additional data, scatter/gather scales to increase responsiveness, to reduce the user-perceived time spent processing a request. We also saw how compute sharding with scatter/gather can be combined with data sharding for large indexes, as well as adding replication to improve reliability and redundancy. Any large-scale distributed system is often a combination of multiple different serving patterns.

本章描述了分散-收集模式这一分布式系统，它用于提升计算速度、减少处理任一特定请求的延迟。前面的服务模式聚焦于为应对额外负载而扩展、或为容纳额外数据而扩展，而分散-收集的扩展目标是提升响应性，减少用户感知到的请求处理耗时。我们还看到，如何把分散-收集的计算分片与面向大型索引的数据分片结合起来，并加入复制以提升可靠性与冗余。任何大规模分布式系统，往往都是多种不同服务模式的组合。
